text:
Duplex escapement, for watches, so called from partaking of the characters of the spur and crown wheels. The axis of balance carries pallet, B, which at every oscillation receives an impulse from the crown teeth. In the axis, A, of balance-wheel is cut a notch into which the teeth round the edge of the wheel successively fall after each one of the crown teeth passes the impulse pallet, B.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 293
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 293; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_293.html.

text:
The pallets, a, b, c, on the wheel rest alternately on the inside and outside of cylinder. To the top of cylinder is attached the balance-wheel. The wheel pallets are beveled so as to keep up the impulse of balance by sliding against the beveled edge of cylinder.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), nos. 294 and 295
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movements 294 and 295; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_294.html.

text:
A single-pin pendulum escapement. The escape-wheel is a very small disk with single eccentric pin; it makes half a revolution for every beat of the pendulum, giving the impulse on the upright faces of the pallets, the horizontal faces of which are dead ones. This can also be adapted to watches.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 305
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 305; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_305.html.

text:
Three-legged pendulum escapement. The pallets are formed in an opening in a plate attached to the pendulum, and the three teeth of the escape-wheel operate on the upper and lower pallets alternately.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 306
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 306; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_306.html.

text:
A detached pendulum escapement, leaving the pendulum, P, free or detached from the escape-wheel, except at the time of receiving the impulse and unlocking the wheel. There is but one pallet, I, which receives impulse only during the vibrations of the pendulum to the left. The lever, Q, locks the escape-wheel until just before the time for giving the impulse, when it is unlocked by the click, C, attached to the pendulum. As the pendulum returns to the right, the click, which oscillates on a pivot, will be pushed aside by the lever.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 308
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 308; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_308.html.

text:
The pendulum plays between the fork-pins, P, Q, and so raises one of the weighted pallets out of the wheel at each vibration. When the pendulum returns the pallet falls with it, and the weight of the pallet gives the impulse.

— Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements (1908), no. 309
provenance: Henry T. Brown, Five Hundred and Seven Mechanical Movements, 21st edition (1908), movement 309; public-domain excerpt. Transcription: https://507movements.com/mm_309.html.
